payload.scope: A human-made time-frequency representation that maps a signal's frequency axis to a logarithmic (or other perceptual) scale so that bins are spaced proportionally to their center frequency. It persists through audio analysis libraries and research implementations that compute the representation from a signal's short-time Fourier transform with frequency-axis resampling.

definition.body: A log-frequency spectrogram is a human-made time-frequency representation that maps a signal's spectrum onto a frequency axis whose spacing is proportional to the logarithm of frequency. payload.name: linear-prediction-coefficient
payload.scope: A human-made set of scalar coefficients that parameterize a linear prediction model for a signal, quantifying how each sample can be estimated as a weighted sum of previous samples. These coefficients form the core representation in speech coding, speaker identification, and spectral analysis.

definition.body: A linear prediction coefficient is a human-made scalar parameter a_k that appears in a linear prediction model where a signal sample x[n] is estimated as a weighted sum of P previous samples: x_hat[n] = sum_{k=1}^{P} a_k x[n-k]. Its parameters are: (1) the prediction order P, determining the number of coefficients, (2) the coefficient values themselves a_1 through a_P, computed via autocorrelation, covariance, or lattice methods, and (3) the normalization convention (whether a_0 = 1 or the coefficients are normalized). It persists through speech coding standards (G.729, ACELP codecs), LPC analysis software (MATLAB lpc, librosa.lpc), and academic implementations across signal processing. e.g.: MATLAB lpc() function output; G.729 CELP codec LSP parameters derived from LPC coefficients; librosa.lpc function output; ITU-T G.721 ADPCM quantizer uses related coefficients | not: linear-prediction-filter (the filter whose transfer function is the reciprocal of the prediction polynomial); reflection-coefficient (parcor coefficients, which are a nonlinear reparameterization of LPC coefficients) [formal: coefficient praedictionis linearis | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes]

payload.name: tempogram
payload.scope: A human-made visual representation that maps tempo periodicity over time by computing onset autocorrelation across a range of lag values

definition.body: Tempogram analysis is a music information retrieval technique that reveals tempo periodicity by computing the self-similarity of an onset envelope over varying lag values. The method operates by: (1) computing an onset detection function from the audio signal, (2) computing onset autocorrelation or inter-onset-interval similarity over a range of lag values, and (3) displaying the result as a two-dimensional map where one axis represents lag (or tempo) and the other represents time. payload.name: beat-detection
payload.scope: A human-made signal processing method that classifies individual audio frames as beat or non-beat positions using local onset energy features

definition.body: Beat detection is a real-time audio analysis technique that classifies each frame of a signal as either a beat position or a non-beat position. The method operates by: (1) computing a short-time energy or spectral flux onset function, (2) applying a running-average threshold or adaptive detector to each frame independently, and (3) outputting a binary classification for every frame. Unlike global beat tracking, it produces no tempo estimate or phase alignment — only a frame-level beat/non-beat decision. Persistence mechanism: implemented as standalone algorithms in DJ software, music analysis libraries, and embedded audio processing systems; taught as a fundamental technique in digital signal processing. e.g.: Kubilius onset detector; McVicar drum detection threshold; Essentia BeatDetector; Tzanetakis beat detector | not: beat-tracking; onset-detection; tempo-estimation [formal: pulsus-detectio | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes]
